the adherence of RBC from diabetics, but not from normal subjects, to endothelial cells results in oxidant stress, PKC activation, and transendothelial cell migration of monocytes.
the adherence of red blood cells from patients with diabetes to endothelial cells induces a cascade of cellular reactions that result in transendothelial diapedesis of leukocytes.

the adherence of diabetes mellitus red blood cells to vascular endothelium induces cellular oxidant stress, which results in protein kinase C activation and platelet endothelial adhesion molecule- 1 phosphorylation.

the interaction of diabetic red blood cells (RRC) with vascular endothelium.

the interaction of diabetic erythrocytes with endothelial cells, and the subsequent transendothelial passage of monocytes, which may contribute to the pathogenesis and progression of vascular complications in diabetes mellitus.
the pathophysiology of diabetes mellitus and the role of oxidative stress in the development of vascular complications in diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diabetic RBC adherence to endothelial cells results in oxidant stress and monocyte transmigration, which may contribute to the pathogenesis and progression of atherosclerosis.

the adherence of RBC to vascular endothelium is the first step in a cascade of events that ultimately results in the transendothelial diapedesis of inflammatory cells, which may play an important initiating role in vascular injury.

the adherence of RBC from diabetic patients to endothelial cells leads to the production of lipid radicals that in turn activate PKC, resulting in PECAM- 1 phosphorylation and increased monocyte transendothelial diapedesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the adherence of RBC from diabetic patients to endothelial cells induces oxidant stress and PKC activation, which results in increased transendothelial cell migration of monocytes, a key step in atherogenesis.
diabetic RBC-induced endothelial cell oxidant stress causes monocyte transendothelial cell migration.
the adherence of RBC to endothelium is an initiating event in atherosclerosis and that the adherence of normal RBC is atheroprotective.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the adherence of hyperglycemia-induced diabetic RBC to vascular endothelial cells leads to the activation of protein kinase C (a key enzyme in the signaling cascade) and phosphorylation of platelet endothelial adhesion molecule- 1 (PECAM1) (a key adhesion molecule) on the surface of vascular endothelial cells, resulting in the transmigration of monocytes (the precursors of macrophages) across vascular endothelial cells.
the adherence of RBCs from diabetics to endothelium causes cellular oxidant stress, resulting in transendothelial diapedesis of inflammatory cells and subsequent endothelial injury.
the interaction of diabetic red blood cells with the vascular endothelium results in a cascade of cellular changes that lead to monocyte migration and adherence to endothelium.
